lesson.found: A first canvas and server were built straight from a one-line request, with no written design: the canvas read MySQL's connection fields by name (host, port, user, databases), so it worked for one engine and would have broken on every other.
lesson.seen: The branch ui-mysql-end-to-end before 2026-11-23, discarded whole; the operator: "fixes is bad planning".
lesson.does: The schema and the spec come first (root method schema, rules the-schema-decides); shared code names no engine's word (rules engine-neutral-shared-code), and every test of shared code runs on every registered engine.

lesson.found: A cleanup was reported done before it was: the co-author lines a coding agent adds by default were still in commits on GitHub, and the repository's contributors showed the agent.
lesson.seen: main before its rewrite of 2026-11-23 (the MySQL engine's merge); the contributors list of the repository.
lesson.does: Rules no-attribution and one-check; every claim in a PR carries the output of the command that proves it (root method pr, the gate table).

lesson.found: The first design kept each engine's data as JSON beside the relational model: the database could check nothing inside it.
lesson.seen: The design session of 2026-11-24, decision relational and its revision.
lesson.does: Every engine's data is in its own tables (root decision cortex-and-engine-schemas); the database enforces every reference (rules the-database-enforces).

lesson.found: The Rust engine_mysql was started as a copy of the Python prototype: its model in the prototype's JSON shape (objects keyed by strings like "shop|table|orders", references as two-element lists, the server's own objects under a fake database "@server") and its writer reproducing the prototype's quirks (a missing value printed as None, Python's own JSON format) so the two outputs could be compared as text. Rust is a different language; the prototype only showed what the engine must do.
lesson.seen: Branch app-engine, commits bbcb144 and 3197f2a, never pushed; the branch deleted and started again from main the same day. The operator: "throw away and redo with the instruction not to do the same copy python shit".
lesson.does: Decisions rust-is-production and python-engine-retired; specs/tasks/SF-156-engine-mysql.xml designs the engine from MySQL's catalog and the plugin's tables, in idiomatic Rust, proven by round trips on live servers and never by matching the prototype's text. Read the prototype for facts only (which catalog table gives what), never for shape.

lesson.found: A wrong design was patched step by step (the writer rewritten, then the model offered a "fix") instead of being thrown away and designed again.
lesson.seen: Branch app-engine on 2026-11-27; the operator: "I do not want any fixed, clean design and performance".
lesson.does: When a design is found wrong, say so, throw the work away and design again from the spec; never offer a fix on top of it.

lesson.found: deny.toml's licence list was written from licences common in Rust, not from the dependencies: three licences no crate used were let in; CI warned.
lesson.seen: PR #163 (the app's store and core in Rust), commits a8ced60 to 33052fb; the operator: "don't guess and create errors".
lesson.does: Nothing is written into the repository from a guess: a list, a version or a name comes from the tool that reports it (tools/app/licences.py for licences, crates.io for versions, the catalog for names), and the reply cites that output.

lesson.found: Clippy's pedantic lints failed the build on backticks in comments, function length and similar style, costing hours of fixes that caught no bug.
lesson.does: The workspace runs clippy's own lints with warnings failing the build, without pedantic (owner's decision).

lesson.found: The agent went quiet for minutes while CI ran without saying what it waited on, and, sent to merge a pull request, opened another one with fixes nobody asked for.
lesson.seen: PRs #161 and #162 (the architecture page); the operator: "don't you ever disappear without telling me".
lesson.does: Before every step, one line: what it is and how long it takes; after it, the result. Do what was asked, nothing more; work found on the way is reported and offered, never started unasked. Name every issue and pull request by number and short description, never a bare number.

lesson.found: The first Rust build's round trip compared design A with design B, read back from the servers. A fact the import lost was missing from both, so the designs compared equal while the servers differed: seven green round trips hid partition options, named subpartitions, a FEDERATED table's remote table, a bare PASSWORD REQUIRE CURRENT and doubled backslashes, and a subpartition's comment moved onto its partition (found the moment the servers' DDL was compared).
lesson.seen: PR #169 (SF-156, the Engine trait and engine_mysql in Rust), its review of 2026-11-28; the owner: "correctness on the other hand is absolute the entire point".
lesson.does: Every engine's round trip compares the servers themselves as well as the designs: each object's DDL as the server writes it (MySQL: SHOW CREATE and SHOW GRANTS) on the source and on the server the written SQL made, identical (decision proof-server-against-server; rules nothing-lost).

lesson.found: Every blocking bug of the first Rust build was in a feature no sample used: a read-only database holding a view, a view calling a function, a check or expression default holding a string, a binary default, bare partition names, a MERGE table across databases, a unique key named like a foreign key, a program under NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES, accounts with password hashes. A round trip proves only what its samples contain.
lesson.seen: PR #169's review; tools/mysql/samples/found.sql and found-8.0.sql now hold each case.
lesson.does: A task's mapping names a sample for every fact it maps and every quirk it handles; a fact no sample exercises is listed in the PR as unproven. A bug found is first a sample, then a fix.

lesson.found: MySQL 8.0's catalog escapes the quotes of CHECK_CLAUSE and of an expression default (_utf8mb4\'a\'), gives a binary default as hex (0x6162), and SHOW CREATE TABLE writes partition names without backticks; information_schema.PARTITIONS gives each subpartition's own comment; 5.7 prints a grant's column list in its own hash order. The parsers' tests passed on SHOW CREATE text written from memory, with backticks the server never writes.
lesson.seen: PR #169's review, each confirmed on a live 8.0 and 5.7 with tools/mysql/show.py.
lesson.does: Every format the code reads is first seen on a live server of each version (tools/mysql/show.py), and every parser test's fixture is that server's text, pasted as it came, with the server and date it came from. A DDL fragment the catalog alters is taken from the server's own DDL.

lesson.found: mysql_async's pool resets each connection when it is returned (reset_connection, on by default), which clears the session. The read's settings (read only, the lock wait, the statement cap, sql_mode, utf8mb4) were set with init, run once per connection, so they held only for each connection's first query; found because a round trip's result changed between runs.
lesson.seen: PR #169, commit d4909e0; mysql_async 0.37.1 src/opts/mod.rs (init runs once, setup after every reset).
lesson.does: Session settings go where the driver re-applies them after every reset (mysql_async: setup), and a test proves a setting holds on a connection's second use. Every engine's task names its driver's behaviour, read from the driver's source.

lesson.found: The spec said an account is kept "never its password or hash", so every account was written back with an empty password: open to anyone who could reach the server. SchemaForge is a tool that can be used for migration; a migration that changes how an account signs in is not one.
lesson.seen: PR #169's review; the owner: "we need to export exact as it is", "the same way as mysqldump would do if I use it for migration".
lesson.does: What is read lands in the store and is written back exactly as the server holds it, account hashes among it (engine_mysql.accounts.auth_string), kept in the database, never in git (decision exact-migration). A gap in the schema is closed by a schema change in a design session, never by dropping or reducing what the server holds.

lesson.found: The task file fixed the writer's order as read-only databases before views and views before routines: a view calling a stored function, or a view or routine in a read-only database, could not load. The order was written as a list, not from what MySQL checks when each statement runs.
lesson.does: A task's writing order is derived from what the server checks at CREATE time (MySQL: CREATE VIEW checks the functions it calls; a routine's body is checked when it runs; a read-only database refuses every CREATE), and a sample exercises each dependency.

lesson.found: A commit was made and pushed while tools/check.py had failed: the command piped the check into tail, whose success hid the check's exit code.
lesson.seen: PR #169, commit d4909e0 (the check passed again on the committed tree, but the commit was not proven when it was made).
lesson.does: A gate's exit code is read on its own, never through a pipe, before anything is committed; the PR carries each gate's exit.

lesson.found: The build session runs tools only (no raw docker, cargo, sed or heredocs), and the agent could not list the containers, reach a server already running, or pass a server option a schema needs, without first writing a tool; it lost time and asked the owner for what a tool should have given.
lesson.seen: PR #169, 2026-11-28; tools/local/containers.py and tools/app/mysql.py's --option and --source were written for it.
lesson.does: A task file names the tools its agent runs and what each does (its tools element); a tool a step needs and the repository lacks is part of the task's owns, written before the step that needs it.
